title: Supply-Chain Knowledge Map — first source-backed resource branches
purpose: Three small source-backed branches for Resource Candidate Card research. They orient opportunity selection and do not choose a post, prove a result, or prescribe organisation-specific policy.

source_capsule.source_locator: Overview of Global Order Promising — overview of promising inputs and alternatives
source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: Oracle describes order promising as evaluating requested or promise dates against supply, capacity, lead time, sourcing and alternatives.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Documents a vendor order-promising model, not a universal promise-control policy.

source_capsule.source_locator: Determine How Order Promising Gets and Estimates Availability — expected purchase-order receipts
source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: Oracle documents that expected purchase-order receipts can be excluded from availability calculations when their reliability is inadequate.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Documents available-to-promise inputs and unreliable-receipt treatment in Oracle; it does not set a universal reliability threshold.

source_capsule.source_locator: Percentage of supplier on-time delivery — measure definition
source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: APQC defines supplier on-time delivery as a measurable supplier-performance input; it does not determine a customer order's service outcome by itself.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Defines a supplier OTD measure; it is not proof of downstream customer service in a named situation.

source_capsule.source_locator: Abstract and literature-review scope — engineer-to-order delivery-date setting
source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: The reviewed delivery-date-setting literature treats delivery commitments as context-dependent; this source's review scope is engineer-to-order.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Delivery-date-setting review is specific to ETO context and cannot be generalised as a universal policy.

source_capsule.source_locator: Lecture 2 — economic order quantity model and assumptions
source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: MIT course material presents EOQ as an inventory model with explicit assumptions and inputs, not as a complete dispatch or consolidation policy.

source_registry.claim_boundary: EOQ is a model with explicit assumptions, not a complete dispatch or consolidation policy.

source_capsule.source_locator: Abstract — quantity-based order consolidation in a multi-item, multi-echelon inventory system
source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: The study models quantity-based consolidation as a setting-specific trade-off among inventory, transport and service effects; it does not produce a universal batch size.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Quantity-based consolidation evidence is model- and setting-bound; it does not calculate a universal batch size.

source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: FHWA frames freight choices as logistics trade-offs; it does not provide a current company or lane benchmark.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Freight trade-off framework gives context, not a current company or lane benchmark.

source_capsule.source_locator: Exception-Based Planning — exception profile and planning-context guidance
source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: SAP documents exception-based planning patterns that use defined deviations and contextual drill-down; this is not independent outcome evidence.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Documents an SAP implementation pattern, not independent proof of planning outcomes.

source_capsule.source_locator: Overview of Plan Exceptions — investigate and resolve exceptions
source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: Oracle documents plan exceptions as objects that can be prioritised, investigated and resolved; severity and ownership remain organisation-specific.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Documents plan-exception investigation and resolution in Oracle; severity and owner remain organisation-specific.

source_capsule.source_locator: Exceptions in a Constrained Supply Plan — named exception conditions
source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: Oracle documents named exception conditions in constrained supply plans; it does not establish that alerts improve service or workload.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Documents named constrained-plan exceptions; it does not prove alerts improve service or workload.

source_capsule.supported_paraphrase: SAP documents an exception-based release pattern, while the operational policy and decision rights remain local.

source_registry.claim_boundary: Documents an exception-based release pattern; local policy and decision rights remain local.

nodes.label: Customer promise at risk

reader_contexts.moment: A changed supplier confirmation is received for an open customer order.

decision_questions: Has a changed supply input actually changed the customer commitment?
boundaries_and_exceptions: Organisation-specific customer communication and escalation ownership are out of scope.
evidence_routes: Order-promising documentation plus locally defined policy.
nodes.not_a_claim: This does not assert that every changed supplier date creates customer risk.
nodes.claim_boundary: Order-promising relationships are source-backed; any local escalation rule needs its own source or an explicitly configurable label.

nodes.label: Supply availability and expected receipt
decision_questions: Which supply inputs can inform the promise calculation?
nodes.not_a_claim: A receipt date alone is not a customer promise.
nodes.claim_boundary: This captures a system relationship, not a claim that every ERP has the same inputs.

nodes.label: Expected receipt reliability and freshness
decision_questions: Can this expected receipt be trusted enough to inform availability?
evidence_routes: Availability documentation and a local reliability policy.
nodes.not_a_claim: No universal reliability threshold is implied.
nodes.claim_boundary: Supplier OTD is an input metric, not an automatic promise decision.

nodes.label: Sourcing and recovery alternatives
decision_questions: Can an alternative supply option change the promise position?
evidence_routes: Order-promising documentation plus a local feasibility check.
nodes.not_a_claim: Alternative sourcing is not assumed feasible, fast, or economical.
nodes.claim_boundary: Alternative sourcing is a possible input to promising, not an outcome guarantee.

nodes.label: Batch versus dispatch decision

reader_contexts.moment: MOQ, freight consolidation and customer service needs conflict.

decision_questions: When does waiting to consolidate stop being economically or service-wise defensible?
boundaries_and_exceptions: A public framework cannot calculate a local batch size without actual inputs.
evidence_routes: EOQ assumptions, consolidation research and organisation-specific input data.
nodes.not_a_claim: This does not prescribe a universal order quantity or shipment date.
nodes.claim_boundary: Model relationships are source-backed; any numeric answer needs local inputs and reproducibility.

nodes.label: Inventory and waiting exposure
decision_questions: What inventory or waiting exposure changes when the batch policy changes?
evidence_routes: EOQ method and local inventory assumptions.
nodes.not_a_claim: Inventory response cannot be inferred without demand, lead-time and policy assumptions.
nodes.claim_boundary: No stock or service result is claimed from this map.

nodes.label: Transport and handling economics
decision_questions: Which cost changes with a smaller or more consolidated shipment?
evidence_routes: Consolidation research and local freight data.
nodes.not_a_claim: A lower rate does not automatically mean lower total cost.
nodes.claim_boundary: External evidence describes trade-offs, not a local freight result.

nodes.label: Customer-service constraint
decision_questions: How long can an order wait before the service condition changes?
evidence_routes: Local customer commitment and a clearly stated scenario.
nodes.not_a_claim: This map has no universal service threshold.
nodes.claim_boundary: The service constraint is a local input, not an external benchmark.

nodes.label: Planning signal or alert

reader_contexts.moment: An alert inbox contains more signals than a human can actively investigate.

decision_questions: Is this a signal to inspect or a material exception that needs an owner?
evidence_routes: Planning-system exception documentation and local policy.
nodes.not_a_claim: Not every system alert deserves interruption.
nodes.claim_boundary: Vendor documentation gives operational patterns, not outcome evidence.

nodes.label: Material exception criteria
decision_questions: What makes a deviation material enough to require human action?
evidence_routes: System exception patterns plus organisation-defined materiality.
nodes.not_a_claim: No fixed alert threshold is claimed.

nodes.label: Accountable recovery action
decision_questions: Who must investigate or decide the next action?
evidence_routes: Exception investigation pattern plus local decision rights.
nodes.not_a_claim: The owner cannot be universalised from a vendor implementation pattern.
nodes.claim_boundary: Decision rights must be labelled as local/configurable in any public object.

nodes.label: Closure evidence and re-alert condition
decision_questions: What evidence closes the exception, and what condition brings it back?
evidence_routes: Exception resolution/release patterns plus local policy.
nodes.not_a_claim: Closing an alert is not proof the underlying risk is eliminated.
nodes.claim_boundary: Closure/re-alert conditions remain local policy design.

edges.claim_boundary: Supply is an input to order promising, not an automatic customer-date change.
Alternative supply is a possible promising input, not assumed recovery.
The trade-off is model/context-bound and needs local inputs for a decision.
The local service condition cannot be inferred from EOQ alone.
EOQ supplies one input relationship, not a dispatch recommendation.
Transport input requires local cost and lane context.
A signal becomes material through local criteria; sources do not define one universal threshold.
Ownership and escalation are local decision rights.
Closure evidence and re-alert condition are local policy design.

branches.label: Supplier confirmation versus customer promise

scope_window.reader_moment: A changed supplier confirmation appears against an open customer order.
scope_window.operating_object_or_signal: Requested date, promised date, supply availability, expected receipt and sourcing option.
scope_window.decision_or_tension: Which changed inputs can genuinely alter the customer promise?
scope_window.reader_payoff: Prepare a more precise conversation about promise risk without treating every supplier input as a customer exception.
scope_window.in_scope: Order-promising relationships and the information needed to assess them.
scope_window.out_of_scope: Universal reliability thresholds, freight economics, and organisation-specific escalation ownership.
scope_window.boundary_or_exception: Any final escalation owner must be explicitly local/configurable.

deep.label: Reliable supply input
deep.purpose: Show why supply availability and receipt reliability are separate inputs.

wide.label: Alternative supply context
wide.purpose: Add a possible alternative input without assuming recovery.

branches.claim_boundary: Source-backed relations can inform a candidate; public policy choices or success claims need further support.

branches.label: Batch, consolidate, or dispatch

scope_window.reader_moment: MOQ, freight-consolidation and customer-service pressures point in different directions.
scope_window.operating_object_or_signal: Order quantity, demand rate, inventory exposure, freight break and service constraint.
scope_window.decision_or_tension: When does waiting to consolidate stop being economically or service-wise defensible?
scope_window.reader_payoff: Separate the inputs to a batch/dispatch choice before using a formula or a freight rate as an answer.
scope_window.in_scope: The inventory, transport and service trade-off.
scope_window.out_of_scope: A universal batch size, local commercial terms, or a numerical recommendation without actual inputs.
scope_window.boundary_or_exception: Any numeric model must state its assumptions and reproduce its calculation.

narrow.label: The choice
narrow.purpose: Show batch versus dispatch as a decision, not a formula.

wide.label: Service constraint
wide.purpose: Add the customer-service condition that limits waiting.

branches.claim_boundary: The branch supports trade-off reasoning, not a numerical answer until local inputs and assumptions are present.

branches.label: Exception policy: signal to accountable action

scope_window.reader_moment: A planning alert inbox contains more signals than can be investigated immediately.
scope_window.operating_object_or_signal: Exception signal, materiality criteria, accountable owner, recovery action and closure evidence.
scope_window.decision_or_tension: Which alert requires interruption, what action is permitted, and what closes or re-opens it?
scope_window.reader_payoff: Turn a noisy exception list into a policy discussion with named decisions and closure logic.
scope_window.in_scope: Exception signal, materiality, owner, action and closure/re-alert relationship.
scope_window.out_of_scope: Universal thresholds, organisational hierarchy, or a claim that exception management improves performance.
scope_window.boundary_or_exception: Severity, decision rights and closure evidence are local design choices.

narrow.label: Signal
narrow.purpose: Start with the signal a planner actually sees.

deep.label: Material exception
deep.purpose: Show the distinction between a signal and materiality.

wide.label: Action and closure
wide.purpose: Show the accountable pathway without claiming a universal owner.

branches.claim_boundary: The branch supports a source-aware policy-design discussion, not outcome claims or a universal alert design.

notes: See references/research/2026-08-07-supply-chain-resource-opportunity-seeds.md for source summaries and limitations. The next entry point is Creative Opportunity Selection, not visual production.
